sources.entry: Graphweaver - Turn multiple data sources into a single GraphQL API. (Source Code) MIT Nodejs

summary.one_liner: Graphweaver is a self-hostable, code-first GraphQL server that connects multiple data sources (databases, SaaS platforms, REST APIs) behind a single GraphQL API with an admin UI.
summary.what_it_does: It generates an instant CRUD GraphQL API from connected data sources such as Postgres, MySQL, SQLite, SaaS platforms and REST endpoints. It supports queries that filter across sources, for example pulling database records based on a name stored in a CRM. Role-based access control, access control lists, row-level and column-level security are built in, along with pre-built identity providers for a local database and Amazon Cognito. An out-of-the-box admin UI lets you view and edit data. A code generator can introspect a database and produce TypeScript resolvers that you can override, since the result is a standard GraphQL server.
use_cases: Build a single GraphQL API over several databases and SaaS tools
Query data that spans multiple sources in one request
Add row and column level permissions to a GraphQL API
Generate a back-office admin panel for existing data
Self-host a GraphQL layer as an alternative to Hasura
Expose a REST API as GraphQL
how_to_run: Choose a project name and a backend (MikroORM PostgreSQL, MikroORM MySQL, or REST)
cd into the new project and run: pnpm install
Start the development server with: pnpm start
Connect a data source via the docs (importing a database or connecting an empty data source)
notable: Code-first design: resolvers can be overridden or customised in ordinary TypeScript
Cross-source filters that join across different data sources
Built-in admin UI generated for managed data
Code generator that creates TypeScript resolvers from database introspection
Row-level and column-level security with RBAC and ACLs
caveats: Requires Node >22 and PNPM >9, and the Node.js-based setup is more involved than a single binary
Pre-built identity providers are limited to Local Database and Amazon Cognito according to the README
Full documentation and examples are hosted on an external docs site rather than in the README
keywords: share data from crm and database
